title: Can scrambling protect quantum state distinguishability under noise?
summary: Quantum state distinguishability is a fundamental concept in quantum information science that underpins a wide range of important practical tasks. Traditionally formulated for pairs of states, quantum state distinguishability is here extended to quantum state ensembles, which we characterize through the average pairwise trace distance.
